message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for a Christian to expect 24/7 supervision of their children because of the campus having all-night security. Hmm, let me break this down. First, I know that as a Christian, there are certain values and teachings that guide behavior. Things like love, responsibility, and trust come to mind. So, the parent is concerned about their children's safety, which is understandable. All-night security might make them feel that constant supervision is necessary. But wait, is 24/7 supervision really the best approach? I mean, children need some independence to grow and learn. If they're constantly supervised, maybe they won't develop the skills they need to handle situations on their own. That could be a problem in the long run. Also, trust is a big part of parenting. If a parent doesn't trust their children, it might affect the child's self-esteem and their ability to make good decisions. Trusting them to handle certain situations can build their confidence and character. I should also consider the teachings of the Bible. There's a lot about raising children in the fear of the Lord, but there's also emphasis on teaching them wisdom and allowing them to learn from their experiences. Proverbs 22:6 says, "Train up a child in the way he should go; even when he is old, he will not depart from it." This suggests that while guidance is important, it's also about equipping them so they can make good choices as they grow. Another point is the role of the church and community. If the campus has all-night security, maybe the parent feels that the environment is safe enough that they don't need to supervise every moment. But relying too much on external security might take away from the parent's responsibility to teach their children about safety and making wise choices. I also wonder about the balance between protection and freedom. It's a fine line. Too much supervision can be stifling, but too little can lead to risky behavior. Each child is different, so the approach should probably be tailored to their individual needs and maturity level. In conclusion, while it's natural to want to protect children, expecting 24/7 supervision might not be the best approach. It's important to foster trust, independence, and wisdom, all while ensuring their safety. As a Christian, relying on God's guidance and teaching children in His ways can help strike that balance.
